To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) differential wiring analysis is a new method to identify the causal mutation in microarray data; 2) it is based on an algorithm that integrates differential expression, transcript abundance and differential wiring into a weighted score; 3) it correctly identified the myostatin mutation as the causal mutation in Piedmontese cattle; and 4) it is applicable to any gene expression study that has microarray data and a known causal mutation.

(a) a new algorithm correctly identifies a causal regulatory mutation by contrasting co-expression networks; (b) this algorithm uses a data-driven, weighted integration of transcript abundance, differential wiring and differential expression; (c) the algorithm is applicable to any species and any trait.
“a differential wiring analysis of expression data correctly identifies the gene with the causal mutation.”

the identification of the causal mutation from gene expression data alone, and the development of a new algorithm to achieve this goal.
a novel, data-driven method to identify causal regulatory differences from microarray data.
the development of a new algorithm that identifies causal regulatory changes from microarray data.

this new method is a powerful tool for identifying causal mutations and their effects on transcriptional networks.
